correctness.rationale: Every unselected all-B triple must be dominated by a selected layer-one vertex sharing a B-pair. Adding one pair per selected all-B triple therefore gives a pair cover of every triple at cost at most the original dominating-set size, including any selection in layer two. The complement is triangle-free, so Mantel gives the claimed lower bound. For the upper witness, an all-B triple contains a same-side pair of the balanced split, a layer-one vertex either has a B element outside W (use layer two) or both inside W (use W), and an unselected layer-two vertex has a same-side partner in B (each split part has size at least two). The three layer sizes add to t_n+n−2; dividing the bounds by n² gives 1/4. This is an exact all-n argument, not an extrapolation from the recorded tests. The verifier and recorded checks concern a finite range of witness sizes and Mantel examples, not exact domination numbers.
